    Analysis

    Analyse systems, trajectories, and measured data by kind of data: series, paths, fields, agents, and networks.

    AlignmentAnalysis(kind='mean-vector', variables=None, *, group=None, vectors=False)

    Bases: BaseAnalysis

    Alignment of the members of a source at every frame, of one kind.

    The members are the agents of a group, the sites of a field, or the columns of a set of series, and each holds an angle or a vector. A trajectory gives the agents of a group with their directions or phases, velocities, and positions, else every frame of a field of angles, or of vectors with vectors=True, else the series of variables or the states with the role 'phase', one column per member and one row per sample.

    • 'mean-vector': the length of the mean unit vector, 1 when every member points the same way and about 1 / sqrt(n) for random directions. It reads vectors when the source has them, and angles otherwise.
    • 'mean-rotation': the mean normalized angular momentum of agents about their centre in a plane, 1 when every agent turns the same way and near 0 for a polarized or disordered group. It reads positions and velocities.
    • 'axial': |<exp(2 i theta)>| of the angles, which ignores the sign of a direction.
    • 'mean-phase': the modulus r and the argument psi of the mean r exp(i psi) = <exp(i theta)> of the angles, the synchrony and the mean phase.
    • 'principal-axis': the eigenvector of the largest eigenvalue of a symmetric tensor at every site, axes_, and the scalar order of the tensor at every site, order_. It reads a field of a symmetric tensor state, or an array of its independent components on the last axis, whose number gives the symmetry and the dimension: 2 and 5 for a symmetric traceless tensor in 2 and 3 dimensions, and 3 and 6 for a symmetric tensor.

    Angles are derived from the first two components of vectors when a source has no angles, and a vector of one component points at the angle 0 or pi by its sign. An array of angles holds one snapshot when it has one dimension, and one frame per row of its first axis otherwise, every other axis indexing members. An array of vectors, with vectors=True, holds the components along its last axis, and one snapshot when it has two dimensions. An array for 'mean-rotation' holds the positions followed by the velocities of every agent along its last axis.

    The path of the agent group of a trajectory, or None for the first one.

    AutomatonAnalysis(kind='injective', *, method='auto', window=None, infinite=False, tries=200, random_state=None, max_radius=2, second=None, configuration=None, site=0, steps=1, windows=None, base=2.0, sweeps=100)

    Bases: BaseAnalysis

    Decisions and measures of a system that is a cellular automaton on a finite universe or holds a subshift.

    The analysis prepares on a System. An automaton is a group of cells with one synchronous and deterministic LocalRuleInteraction, and it is linear when the rule is a LinearRuleSpec. The number of values of a cell comes from the finite domain of the state, or else from the rule. A subshift is a group with a state whose domain is a SubshiftSpec.

    • 'injective', 'surjective', and 'pre-injective': whether two different configurations never share their image, whether every configuration has a preimage, which on a finite universe holds exactly when it is injective, and whether two configurations that differ only inside a window never share their image. Small universes are decided by enumerating every configuration, and larger ones by a SAT encoding solved by PySAT. A linear automaton is decided from its matrix, all three holding exactly when the matrix is invertible, or on Z^d from its Laurent polynomial, injective when it is a monomial and surjective and pre-injective when it is not zero.
    • 'garden-of-eden': a pattern on a window that no configuration maps to. Small universes enumerate the images of every configuration, and larger ones draw random patterns and keep the first one whose preimage constraints a SAT solver finds unsatisfiable.
    • 'inverse': an automaton whose composition with a reversible automaton is the identity, with the smallest memory. The search tries the neighbourhoods of every radius up to max_radius, a box of offsets on a lattice or the ball of group elements on a group space, and keeps the first on which the image determines every cell.
    • 'compose': the automaton that applies the automaton and then second on the same space, whose neighbourhood holds the composite t s of every element t read by the second and s read by the first.
    • 'difference': where two runs differ when one starts from configuration and the other from it with the cell at site changed to its next value modulo the number of states.
    • 'entropy': the entropy log |X_F| / |F| of the configurations of a subshift, or of the image of an automaton whose rule and neighbourhood are applied on every window. X_F is the set of admissible configurations of a window F, or the set of images on the sites of F whose cells lie inside it. Along a Følner sequence of windows the values approach the topological entropy.
    • 'matrix': the square matrix of a linear automaton over its field, whose row g gives the image at g.
    • 'polynomial': the Laurent polynomial sum a_s x^s of a linear automaton on a lattice, its symbol on Z^d.
    • 'admissible' and 'violations': whether no forbidden pattern appears in configuration, and the sites at which one appears.
    • 'count': the number of admissible configurations of the space of a subshift, by dynamic programming over its sites. The counts of completions are shared between assignments that agree on the earlier sites that later patterns read, so a window of a one-dimensional subshift costs linear time.
    • 'sample': an admissible configuration drawn by a Markov chain of single-cell moves that keep it admissible, from configuration, or from every cell at 0.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    kind str

    The decision or measure, one of the kinds above.

    		 'injective'
    method str

    		 'auto'
    window Sequence[int] | None

    The sites where configurations may differ, or of the Garden of Eden pattern, or None for every site.

    		 None

    		 False
    tries int

    		 200
    random_state int | Generator | None

    The seed or generator of the random patterns or of the moves of a sample.

    		 None
    max_radius int

    The largest radius of the memory of the inverse.

    		 2
    second System | None

    The system of the automaton applied after the analysed one.

    		 None
    configuration ArrayLike | None

    The values of the sites: the initial ones of the difference pattern or of a sample, or the ones checked.

    		 None

    The site of the changed cell.

    		 0

    >>> from typing import Annotated
>>> from sage.sets.finite_enumerated_set import FiniteEnumeratedSet
>>> from skcomplex.core.analysis import AutomatonAnalysis
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.elements import Element, LatticeElement
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.interactions import LocalRuleInteraction
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.spaces import BoxNeighborhood, LatticeNeighborhood, LatticeSpace
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.system import System
>>> from skcomplex.core.specs import StateSpec, SubshiftSpec, TableSpec, TotalisticSpec
>>> class CellElement(Element):
...     def __init__(self, label, alive: Annotated[float, StateSpec(domain=FiniteEnumeratedSet([0, 1]))] = 0):
...         super().__init__(label)
...         self.alive = alive
>>> def automaton(size, rule, neighborhood):
...     cells = LatticeElement('cells', element=CellElement, space=LatticeSpace(size))
...     interaction = LocalRuleInteraction(
...         'rule', target='cells', state='alive', rule=rule, neighborhood=neighborhood
...     )
...     return System(elements=[cells], interactions=[interaction])
>>> shift = automaton(8, TableSpec({(1,): 1}), LatticeNeighborhood(((1,),)))
>>> AutomatonAnalysis().prepare(shift).run().injective_
True
>>> majority = automaton(5, TotalisticSpec(lambda total: total >= 2), BoxNeighborhood())
>>> AutomatonAnalysis('garden-of-eden').prepare(majority).run().pattern_.tolist()
[0, 0, 1, 0, 1]
>>> class GoldenCellElement(Element):
...     def __init__(
...         self,
...         label,
...         alive: Annotated[
...             float, StateSpec(domain=SubshiftSpec(LatticeNeighborhood(((0,), (1,))), ((1, 1),)))
...         ] = 0,
...     ):
...         super().__init__(label)
...         self.alive = alive
>>> window = LatticeSpace(6, boundary='fixed')
>>> golden = System(elements=[LatticeElement('cells', element=GoldenCellElement, space=window)])
>>> AutomatonAnalysis('count').prepare(golden).run().count_
21
>>> analysis = AutomatonAnalysis('entropy', windows=[LatticeSpace(20, boundary='fixed')])
>>> analysis.prepare(golden).run().entropy_.round(3).tolist()
[0.706]

    BaseAnalysis

    Bases: BaseConfig[Source, object], ABC

    Base of every analysis: it stores its settings, validates them and prepares on a source, and runs.

    A child stores its settings in __init__ and implements four hooks that the verbs call:

    • _check() validates the settings.
    • _get_data_kind() returns the kind of data the analysis reads, such as 'series' or 'field'.
    • _prepare(source) reads the data from the source with the readers of the base and sets the attributes that end in _.
    • _run() computes the results and sets them as attributes that end in _.

    The readers _read_series, _read_path, _read_fields, _read_snapshots, and _read_networks take a trajectory, and pass an array or a graph through.

    Examples:

    >>> import numpy as np
>>> from skcomplex.core.analysis import BaseAnalysis
>>> class MeanAnalysis(BaseAnalysis):
...     def __init__(self, variables=None):
...         self.variables = variables
...
...     def _get_data_kind(self):
...         return 'series'
...
...     def _prepare(self, source):
...         self.series_ = self._read_series(source, self.variables)
...
...     def _run(self, inputs):
...         self.mean_ = self.series_.values.mean(axis=0)
>>> MeanAnalysis().prepare(np.array([1.0, 2.0, 3.0])).run().mean_.tolist()
[2.0]

    CellComplexAnalysis(kind, space=None, variables=None)

    Bases: BaseAnalysis

    Hodge decomposition of an edge state, Betti numbers of a complex, or curved faces of an angle state.

    It reads a state of a group on a cell complex from a trajectory, or an array with the complex passed as space. An array of one dimension holds one snapshot, and an array of two dimensions one frame per row. Every result has one row per frame.

    The kind 'hodge' writes an edge state as the sum of the exterior derivative of a site potential, the transposed incidence of a face potential, and a remainder that both incidences map to 0. The three parts are orthogonal. The kind 'betti' reads the complex alone. The kind 'curvature' compares the oriented sum of an angle state around every face with the multiples of the period of the state, or of 2 pi for an array.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    kind str

    'hodge', 'betti', or 'curvature'.

    		 required
    space CellComplexSpace | None

    The cell complex, or None for the complex of the group of variables on a trajectory.

    		 None
    variables str | None

    The dotted name of the state of a trajectory, or None for a source that is an array.

    		 None

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    betti_ tuple[int, ...]

    The Betti numbers of every degree, for the kind 'betti'.
    gradient_ Array

    The part of every frame that is the exterior derivative of a site potential, for the kind 'hodge'.
    curl_ Array

    The part of every frame that the transposed incidence of a face potential gives, for the kind 'hodge'.
    harmonic_ Array

    The remainder of every frame, for the kind 'hodge'.
    potential_ Array

    The site potential of every frame, of zero mean, for the kind 'hodge'.
    share_ Array

    The share of the faces of every frame that are curved, for the kind 'curvature'.
    energy_ Array

    The sum over the faces of every frame of one minus the cosine of the oriented sum, for the kind 'curvature'.
    complex_ CellComplexSpace

    The cell complex the analysis reads.
    values_ CellComplexSpace

    The values of the source, with one row per frame.
    period_ CellComplexSpace

    The period of the values.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    AnalysisError

    The kind is unknown, the source names no state of a cell complex, or the values do not fit the complex.

    Examples:

>>> from skcomplex.core.analysis import CellComplexAnalysis
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.spaces import CellComplexSpace, LatticeSpace
>>> space = CellComplexSpace(LatticeSpace((4, 4))).prepare()
>>> CellComplexAnalysis('betti', space=space).prepare().run().betti_
(1, 2, 1)
>>> uniform = np.r_[np.ones(16), np.zeros(16)]
>>> hodge = CellComplexAnalysis('hodge', space=space).prepare(uniform).run()
>>> bool(np.allclose(hodge.harmonic_[0], uniform))
True

    ClusterAnalysis(kind='labels', variables=None, *, periodic=False, diagonal=False, axis=0, radius=None)

    Bases: BaseAnalysis

    Clusters of the occupied cells of a grid, the components of a graph, or the contacts of points, of one kind.

    The grid is a boolean array of any dimension, the last frame of a field of a trajectory, or a graph, the last network of a trajectory. Cells are connected through shared faces, or also corners with diagonal=True.

    With a radius, the source holds points instead, an array with one row per point, a stack of such arrays for the kind 'spanning', or the positions of a group of a trajectory in its last frame. Points closer than twice the radius are connected, and a cluster joins two opposite faces along axis when it holds points within the radius of both. The faces are those of the space of a trajectory, and those of the bounding box of an array.

    • 'labels': the label of every cell and the size of every cluster of a grid, in label order, and whether a cluster joins the two opposite edges of axis.
    • 'sizes': the size of every cluster of a grid or of every component of a graph, largest first.
    • 'percolation': the cluster sizes, the strength of the largest cluster, the mean cluster size, and spanning.
    • 'spanning': the share of the grids of an ensemble, stacked on the first axis or the frames of a trajectory, with a cluster joining the opposite edges of axis.

    CoarseGrainAnalysis(shape=(32, 32), *, box=None, values=None, over=None, state=None)

    Bases: BaseAnalysis

    Agents coarse-grained into a field on a grid, or members into a density over the values of a state.

    An array holds one snapshot, one row per agent in the box. A trajectory gives the positions of its first agent or particle group at every frame, in the box of its space unless box is set, and one grid per frame.

    With over, the analysis coarse-grains in state space instead: every member counts at the given value nearest to its value of a state, and the field is the fraction of members at every value, which sums to 1. An array holds the values of one snapshot, one per member, or one row per frame, and a trajectory gives the values of the state state at every frame. The densities are the initial values of a distribution site group with one member per value.

    CollapseAnalysis(kind='scaling', *, parameters=None, critical=None, nu=None, exponent=0.0, fit=(), waiting=None, lags=None, ratios=None)

    Bases: BaseAnalysis

    Collapse of curves or distributions of several sizes or ages onto one, of one kind.

    The kinds read the curves or the samples of every size or age:

    • 'scaling': the finite-size scaling collapse of curves y_L(p) = L^a f((p - p_c) L^(1/nu)) of every size L, against the control parameters, with the names of fit among 'critical', 'nu', and 'exponent' fitted by minimizing the quality.
    • 'aging': how far correlation curves of several waiting times stay apart against the lag and against tau / t_w, from one curve per waiting time, as the two-time correlation of CorrelationAnalysis gives them.
    • 'distribution': the densities t P(tau, t) of samples of tau at several ages t against tau / t, which collapse under aging.
    • 'crossings': where the curves of consecutive sizes cross against the control parameters, by linear interpolation of their difference, such as the Binder cumulants of several lattice sizes at the critical point.

    Parameters:

    kind str

    The collapse to compute, one of the kinds above.

    The critical value, or the starting value of a fit.

    		 None

    The exponent a of the scaled curves y L^-a, such as gamma / nu for a susceptibility, or the starting value of a fit.

    fit Sequence[str]

    The names among 'critical', 'nu', and 'exponent' to fit.

    The waiting times of the curves of 'aging'.

    The lags shared by every curve of 'aging'.

>>> from skcomplex.core.analysis import CollapseAnalysis
>>> grid = np.linspace(-1, 1, 401)

>>> CollapseAnalysis('crossings', parameters=[1.0, 2.0, 3.0]).prepare(curves).run().crossings_.tolist()

    ComplexityAnalysis(variables=None, *, dimension=6, delay=1, ties='order', random_state=None)

    Bases: BaseAnalysis

    Place of every series of a source, or of every frame of a field, on Rosso's complexity-entropy plane.

    The entropy is the normalized permutation entropy of the ordinal patterns, and the complexity is that entropy times the Jensen-Shannon divergence of the patterns from uniform ones, computed with ordpy. Noise has entropy near 1 and complexity near 0, regular series both near 0, and chaos lies in between with high complexity.

    ties str

    random_state int | None

>>> from skcomplex.core.analysis import ComplexityAnalysis
>>> noise = np.random.default_rng(0).standard_normal(50_000)

>>> plane.entropy_.round(2).tolist(), plane.complexity_.round(2).tolist()

    CorrelationAnalysis(kind='auto', variables=None, *, max_lag=None, dt=1.0, waiting=None, lags=None, connected=False, max_distance=None, method='moment', spacing=1.0, frames=False)

    Bases: BaseAnalysis

    Correlation of every series of a source, of an ensemble at two times, or of a field in space, of one kind.

    The kinds read series, ensembles, or fields:

    • 'auto': the autocorrelation of every series at lags 0 to max_lag, computed with the FFT, and its integrated autocorrelation time dt (1/2 + Σ r(k)), summed to the first negative correlation.
    • 'two-time': the two-time correlation C(t_w + tau, t_w) = <x(t_w) x(t_w + tau)> of an ensemble with one row per run and one column per frame, any further axes, such as sites, averaged over.
    • 'function': the radially averaged spatial correlation of a field on a periodic grid, 1 at distance 0.
    • 'length': the correlation length of a field. The 'moment' method fits the Ornstein-Zernike form 1 / S(q) ∝ 1 + xi² Σ 4 sin²(q_i / 2) over the modes with q̂² xi² <= 1, and the 'fit' method fits C(r) ~ r^-a exp(-r / xi). Several frames are taken as fluctuations about their common mean.
    • 'overlap': the overlap q = <s_i t_i> of two configurations s and t of the same sites, ±1 for identical or reversed configurations of ±1 values and near 0 for independent ones, per frame for frames. It reads a pair of trajectories, whose fields it compares at every frame, or two arrays stacked on the first axis.

    The kinds 'function' and 'length' read the last frame of a trajectory, or every frame when frames is true.

    		 'moment'

    The distance between neighbouring sites.

    DefectAnalysis(period=np.pi, variables=None, *, periodic=True)

    Bases: BaseAnalysis

    Point defects of a two-dimensional field of angles, with their topological charges, at every frame.

    The winding around a plaquette of four neighbouring sites is the sum of the differences of the angles along its edges, each wrapped to one period around 0, over 2 pi. A plaquette with a winding that is not 0 holds a defect of that charge. The charges of a periodic lattice sum to 0.

    An array of two dimensions holds one snapshot, and an array of three dimensions one frame per row of its first axis.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    period float

    The period of the angles, np.pi for axes without head and tail and 2 * np.pi for vectors.

    		 pi
    variables Sequence[str] | None

    The field of a trajectory to read, or None for its first field.

    		 None
    periodic bool

    Whether the lattice joins its opposite edges, or has plaquettes only between its sites.

    		 True

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    angles_

    The angles, with one frame per row of the first axis.
    positions_ list[Array]

    The centres of the plaquettes with a defect at every frame, each an array of defects by dimensions.
    charges_ list[Array]

    The charges of the defects at every frame, each an array in the order of positions_.

    Examples:

    >>> import numpy as np
>>> from skcomplex.core.analysis import DefectAnalysis
>>> rows, columns = np.meshgrid(np.arange(8.0), np.arange(8.0), indexing='ij')
>>> vortex = np.arctan2(rows - 3.5, columns - 3.5)
>>> defects = DefectAnalysis(2 * np.pi, periodic=False).prepare(vortex).run()
>>> defects.positions_[0].tolist(), defects.charges_[0].tolist()
([[3.5, 3.5]], [1.0])

    Bases: BaseAnalysis

    Analyses that apply to a trajectory, a system, or an array, listed under the kind of data they read.

    Preparing reads the kinds of data the source holds. Running builds every analysis of the library that takes no required setting, once per kind of a family, asks each for its data kind, and keeps those whose kind the source holds. A one-dimensional array is one series, and an array of more dimensions is one field and a set of series, one per column.

    Examples:

    >>> import numpy as np
>>> from skcomplex.core.analysis import DiscoveryAnalysis
>>> discovery = DiscoveryAnalysis().prepare(np.zeros((16, 16))).run()
>>> discovery.kinds_
['field', 'series']
>>> discovery.readings_['series']
'every column of the array as a series'
>>> any(type(item).__name__ == 'EntropyAnalysis' for item in discovery.analyses_['series'])

    DistributionAnalysis(kind='histogram', variables=None, *, group=None, bins=30, log=False, absolute=False, orders=(4, 2), tail=10)

    Bases: BaseAnalysis

    Distribution of the values of a source, of one kind.

    The source gives samples as columns: the series of a trajectory or an array, or the speeds of the agents of a trajectory, one sample per frame. The first kinds pool every sample into one:

    • 'histogram': the edges and the probability density of bins bins, equally spaced in the logarithm of the values with log=True for heavy tails.
    • 'ccdf': the complementary cumulative distribution, the share of samples at or above every distinct value.
    • 'gini': the Gini coefficient of nonnegative values, 0 for equality and close to 1 when one holds everything.
    • 'tail-index': the Hill estimate of the tail index from the tail largest positive samples, the exponent alpha - 1 of the survival function of a density p(x) ∝ x^-alpha.

    The other kinds describe every sample:

    • 'moments': the mean, the variance, the skewness, and the excess kurtosis of every sample, or of its absolute values with absolute=True.
    • 'moment-ratio': the ratio <x^p> / <x^q>^(p / q) of the moments of the even orders (p, q), and the cumulant 1 - ratio / ratio_gauss, normalized by the ratio of a centred Gaussian so that it is 0 for Gaussian samples. For the orders 4 and 2 the ratio is the kurtosis about 0 and the cumulant 1 - <x^4> / (3 <x^2>^2), 2/3 for samples at ±1.
    • 'dispersion-index': the variance over the mean of every sample of counts, 1 for Poisson counts, above 1 for overdispersed and below 1 for underdispersed counts.
    • 'records': the number of records of every series, the values larger than every value before them, about the harmonic number of the length for independent values.
    • 'total-variation': the total variation distance 1/2 Σ_u |a_u / A - b_u / B| between the distributions of two groups across units, from one row per item with its group and its unit, 0 for identical distributions and 1 for disjoint ones.

    		 False
    absolute bool

    		 False

    DomainAnalysis(kind='size', variables=None, *, method='moment', spacing=1.0, fit_range=None, times=None, attribute='state')

    Bases: BaseAnalysis

    Domains of every frame of a field, or of the states on a network, of one kind.

    The kinds read frames of a field on a periodic grid:

    • 'size': the characteristic domain size, 2 pi / <k> over the structure factor with method='moment', or the first zero of the correlation function with method='zero'.
    • 'growth': the domain size of every frame and the exponent of its growth in time, the slope of log size against log time over the fit range, 1/2 for non-conserved and 1/3 for conserved order parameters.
    • 'wavelength': the dominant wavelength and wavenumber of a pattern, the peak of its structure factor, and the nematic order of the wave vectors near the peak, 1 for parallel stripes and near 0 for labyrinths or spots.
    • 'interface-density': the share of neighbouring pairs, on a periodic grid without corners or along the edges of a network, whose states differ, 0 for one domain and 1/2 for random binary states.

    A trajectory gives the frames of a lattice state and their times. An array is one frame, or one frame per entry of times along its first axis. A graph carries the states on its nodes for 'interface-density'.

    Bases: BaseAnalysis

    Exact enumeration of the generators of the steady-state cone {v : S v = 0, v_irr >= 0} of a linear program.

    A system gives the program of its linear program law at its initial values, whose bounds give the directions: a negative lower bound makes a variable reversible, a nonpositive upper bound reverses its column, and a variable fixed at zero is removed. A matrix gives the cone directly, with the indices of its irreversible columns.

    • 'modes': the steady-state vectors of minimal support in which every irreversible variable runs in its declared direction. Every reversible column splits in two, the extreme rays of the split cone come from the Parma Polyhedra Library, the two-cycles of split pairs drop, and the rest maps back (Gagneur and Klamt 2004).
    • 'pathways': the generators of the cone with every reversible internal column split and each exchange kept as one column, of either sign when it is reversible (Schilling et al. 2000), and without any generator that is a non-negative combination of the others (Raman 2021, Section 9.8). The generators that run in both directions leave modes_ for lines_.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    kind str

    The generators to enumerate, 'modes' or 'pathways'.

    		 'modes'
    normalize str | None

    The name of a variable to scale every row to one where it is not zero, or None for the smallest integer vector.

    		 None
    exchanges Sequence[str] | None

    The names of the exchange variables, or None for the variables in one row.

    		 None
    timeout float

    The time limit of the enumeration in seconds.

    		 60.0
    labels Sequence[str] | None

    The names of the columns of a matrix, or None for v0, v1, and so on.

    		 None
    irreversible Sequence[int] | None

    The indices of the irreversible columns of a matrix, or None for every column.

    		 None
    sort str | None

    The name of a variable to order the rows by, largest first, such as the growth flux of modes normalised to the uptake, which orders them by yield, or None for a fixed order.

    		 None

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    modes_

    One row per generator, scaled to normalize or to the smallest integer vector, as fractions.
    labels_

    The name of every column of modes_.
    lines_

    The generators that run in both directions, the lines of a cone that is not pointed, one row per line.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    AnalysisError

    The kind is unknown, the right side of a balance is not zero, a coefficient is not close to a fraction, or no system or matrix holds a program, raised by prepare.
    EnumerationLimitError

    The enumeration does not finish within the time limit, raised by run.

    Examples:

    >>> import numpy as np
>>> from skcomplex.core.analysis import ElementaryModeAnalysis
>>> matrix = np.array([[1.0, -1.0, 0.0], [0.0, 1.0, -1.0]])
>>> analysis = ElementaryModeAnalysis(normalize='v0').prepare(matrix).run()
>>> analysis.modes_.tolist()
[[Fraction(1, 1), Fraction(1, 1), Fraction(1, 1)]]

    EmergenceAnalysis(kind='causal', variables=None, *, partition=None, weighting='uniform', search='greedy', lag=1, history=1, estimator='plugin', k=3, base=2.0)

    Bases: BaseAnalysis

    Emergence of a macro scale over a micro scale, of one kind.

    The kinds read a transition matrix or the series of micro variables:

    • 'effective-information': the effective information of a transition matrix, H(mean row) - mean H(row) over the states with observed transitions, split into determinism and degeneracy. A matrix of counts is normalised by row first.
    • 'causal': the causal emergence of a transition matrix, the gain in effective information of the macro matrix of a given or searched partition over the micro matrix. The macro matrix sums the micro transitions from every block to every block, weighting the micro states of a block uniformly, as Hoel, Albantakis, and Tononi (2013) do, or by the stationary distribution, as Klein and Hoel (2020) do. The greedy search of Klein and Hoel (2020) merges the pair of blocks with the largest macro effective information while that grows, so it can miss the best partition. The exhaustive search tries every partition of at most 10 states.
    • 'criteria': the criteria Ψ, Δ, and Γ of Rosas et al. (2020) for the macro feature of the micro series given by partition, estimated lag steps ahead with the minimum mutual information redundancy.
    • 'closure': how well the macro past and the micro past of the macro series given by partition predict the macro future. The coarse-graining is closed when the gap is zero up to the bias of the plug-in estimator.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    kind str

    The emergence to measure, one of the kinds above.

    		 'causal'
    variables Sequence[str] | None

    The micro variables of a trajectory to read, or None for every scalar series.

    		 None
    partition Partition | None

    The macro label of every integer micro state, numbered 0, 1, and so on, or a function from an array of micro states, or from the micro series with one column per variable, to their macro labels. None to search a partition of the matrix.

    		 None
    weighting str

    'uniform' or 'stationary', the weight of the micro states within a block.

    		 'uniform'
    search str

    'greedy' or 'exhaustive', the search when no partition is given.

    		 'greedy'
    lag int

    The number of steps between the present and the future of the criteria.

    		 1
    history int

    The number of past steps the closure conditions on.

    		 1
    estimator str

    'plugin' for the frequencies of symbols, 'gaussian' for the closed form of a fitted Gaussian, or 'knn' for nearest-neighbour conditional mutual informations.

    		 'plugin'
    k int

    The number of neighbours of the 'knn' estimator.

    		 3
    base float

    The base of the logarithm, 2 for bits.

    		 2.0

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    matrix_

    The micro transition matrix, for 'effective-information' and 'causal'.
    values_

    The micro series, one column per micro variable, for 'criteria' and 'closure'.
    labels_

    The label of every micro series.
    information_

    The effective information in bits, for 'effective-information'.
    determinism_

    log2 n minus the mean entropy of the rows, high when every state has one successor.
    degeneracy_

    log2 n minus the entropy of the mean row, high when many states share a successor.
    states_

    The states with observed transitions, the rows the effective information uses.
    partition_

    The macro label of every micro state, for 'causal'.
    macro_matrix_

    The macro transition matrix of the partition, every row summing to one.
    micro_information_

    The effective information of the micro matrix.
    macro_information_

    The effective information of the macro matrix.
    gain_

    The macro minus the micro effective information in bits.
    psi_

    I(V_t ; V_t') - Σ_j I(X_t^j ; V_t'), positive when the macro feature predicts its own future beyond what every micro variable does, a sufficient condition for causal emergence.
    delta_

    max_j [I(V_t ; X_t'^j) - Σ_i I(X_t^i ; X_t'^j)], positive when the macro feature predicts a micro variable beyond the micro variables, a sufficient condition for downward causation.
    gamma_

    max_j I(V_t ; X_t'^j), zero for a causally decoupled feature when psi_ is positive.
    macro_uncertainty_

    H(V_t | V_past), the entropy of the macro future given the macro past.
    micro_uncertainty_

    H(V_t | X_past), the entropy of the macro future given the micro past.
    gap_

    The information the micro past adds about the macro future, zero for a closed coarse-graining.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    AnalysisError

    The matrix is not square or has no observed transition, the partition is not valid, or the exhaustive search gets more than 10 states.

    Warns:

    Type Description
    UnobservedStatesWarning

    Some rows of the micro matrix hold no transition, and the warning names their states.

    Examples:

    >>> import numpy as np
>>> from skcomplex.core.analysis import EmergenceAnalysis
>>> EmergenceAnalysis('effective-information').prepare(np.eye(4)).run().information_
2.0
>>> matrix = np.zeros((4, 4))
>>> matrix[:3, :3], matrix[3, 3] = 1 / 3, 1.0
>>> found = EmergenceAnalysis('causal').prepare(matrix).run()
>>> found.partition_.tolist(), round(found.gain_, 3)
([0, 0, 0, 1], 0.189)
>>> micro = np.random.default_rng(0).integers(0, 4, 5000)
>>> round(EmergenceAnalysis('closure', partition=[0, 0, 1, 1]).prepare(micro).run().gap_, 2)
0.0

    EntropyAnalysis(kind='shannon', variables=None, *, order=2.0, base=2.0, probabilities=False, dimension=3, delay=1, tolerance=0.2, scales=tuple(range(1, 11)), normalize=True, dt=1.0, measure='shannon', ties='order', random_state=None, reference=None)

    Bases: BaseAnalysis

    Entropy of every series of a source, or of every frame of a field, of one kind.

    The kinds read symbols, patterns, or real values:

    • 'shannon', 'renyi', and 'tsallis': the entropy of the distribution of the symbols, or of a probability vector with probabilities=True, the Rényi order and the Tsallis index given by order.
    • 'block', 'rate', and 'excess': the block entropies S_0 to S_m, the entropy rate, and the excess entropy of the blocks of up to dimension symbols, or of square patches of a field.
    • 'lempel-ziv': the number of new phrases of the LZ76 parsing.
    • 'permutation': the entropy of the ordinal patterns of length dimension, or of the windows (columns, rows) of a field, measured with measure.
    • 'sample' and 'approximate': the regularity of patterns of length dimension, close within tolerance standard deviations.
    • 'multiscale': the sample entropy of the means of non-overlapping windows of every scale of scales.
    • 'spectral': the Shannon entropy of the normalized periodogram.
    • 'ensemble': the Shannon entropy in bits of the outcomes of an ensemble at every frame, and their Kullback-Leibler divergence from the reference law, as in the H-theorem. The ensemble has one row per run and one column per frame of integer outcomes, such as ExperimentResult.ensemble returns.

    ErgodicityAnalysis(kind='breaking', variables=None, *, start=0.01, dt=1.0, bins=None, value_range=None, edges=None, samples=100)

    Bases: BaseAnalysis

    Ergodicity of an ensemble of runs, or invariant density of a map or a flow, of one kind.

    The ensemble kinds read one row per run and one column per time, such as ExperimentResult.ensemble returns:

    • 'breaking': the variance across runs of the time averages over the variance of all the values, near 0 for ergodic runs longer than their relaxation time and near 1 when every run is frozen in its own state.
    • 'metric': the fluctuation metric of Thirumalai and Mountain, the mean square deviation of the running time averages from their ensemble mean, which decays as 1 / t for ergodic runs and levels off for frozen ones.
    • 'distance': the median total-variation distance between the values one run visits over time and the values of all runs, after Lesmana et al. (2026), near 0 for ergodic runs and near 1 - p when every run stays in its own state of ensemble weight p.

    The density kinds read one coordinate of a long run, or a one-dimensional map:

    • 'invariant-density': the histogram density of the values of a long run.
    • 'ulam': the Markov chain of a map coarse-grained on the cells between edges by Ulam's method, and the density of its stationary vector.

    times_

    metric_

    EventAnalysis(kind='detect', variables=None, *, threshold=0.0, window=None, start=0.0, end=None, max_step=40, dt=1.0)

    Bases: BaseAnalysis

    Events of one series or of event times, of one kind.

    The kinds read one series or the times of events:

    • 'detect': the events of a series, every maximal run of consecutive values above threshold, with their starts, sizes, durations, peaks, and the waiting times between them. For avalanches recorded as topplings per drive step, an event is an avalanche and its size is the total number of topplings.
    • 'counts': the number of events in consecutive windows of length window, from the times of the events, or from the jump times of a discrete state of a trajectory.
    • 'laminar-durations': the durations of the laminar phases of a series, the complete runs of values within threshold of 0 between two bursts, such as the distance from an invariant manifold of on-off intermittency.
    • 'excursions': the excursions of a series above threshold, every maximal run of values above it, with the profile of every excursion, its values minus the threshold, its size, the sum of the profile, and its duration, the number of its samples. A sequence of records with a size and a duration, such as the cascade records of a lattice, holds excursions already.
    • 'branching': the branching ratio of the series by the multistep regression estimator of mrestimator, which fits r_k ∝ m^k to the regression slopes r_k of the values k steps apart, and stays unbiased when only a fraction of the units is observed. Every series is one trial.

    Times are the times of a trajectory, and the step indices of an array.

    Parameters:

    FitAnalysis(law='power', variables=None, *, group=None, minimum=None, maximum=None, discrete=False, bootstrap=100, candidates=50, compare_with=ALTERNATIVES, block=None, fixed=None, simulations=199, random_state=0)

    Bases: BaseAnalysis

    Law fitted to the values of a source, pooled into one sample.

    The source gives the series of a trajectory or an array, or the speeds of the agents of a trajectory at every frame.

    The laws are:

    • 'power': a power law p(x) ∝ x^-alpha fitted to the tail of the positive samples by maximum likelihood, with Clauset, Shalizi, and Newman's method. The lower cutoff minimises the Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance between the tail and the fit, unless minimum fixes it. The goodness of fit is the share of bootstrap samples whose distance exceeds the data's, and the power law is compared with every alternative of compare_with by a likelihood-ratio test. Discrete samples use the exact discrete likelihood. The warnings of powerlaw about its optimiser are silenced during the run.
    • 'stable': the Lévy stable law fitted by McCulloch's quantile method, in SciPy's S1 parameterization.
    • 'extreme-value': the generalized extreme-value law fitted by maximum likelihood to the maxima of blocks of block samples.
    • 'exponential', 'normal', 'lognormal', 'gamma', 'maxwell', 'rayleigh', and 'uniform': the named law with its free parameters fitted, tested with a Monte Carlo Kolmogorov-Smirnov test that accounts for the fit.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    law str

    The law to fit, one of the laws above.

    		 'power'
    variables Sequence[str] | None

    The variables of a trajectory to read, or None for every scalar series.

    		 None
    group str | None

    The path of the agent or particle group whose speeds are read, or None for the series of a trajectory, or the first group of a trajectory without series.

    		 None
    minimum float | None

    A fixed lower cutoff of the power law, or None to choose it.

    		 None
    maximum float | None

    A fixed upper cutoff of the power law, or None for none.

    		 None
    discrete bool

    Whether the samples of the power law are integers, such as avalanche sizes.

    		 False
    bootstrap int

    The number of bootstrap samples for the p-value of the power law, 0 for none.

    		 100
    candidates int

    The largest number of lower cutoffs tried.

    		 50
    compare_with Sequence[str]

    The alternatives the power law is compared with, among 'exponential', 'lognormal', 'stretched_exponential', and 'truncated_power_law'.

    		 ALTERNATIVES
    block int | None

    The number of samples per block of the extreme-value law.

    		 None
    fixed Mapping[str, float] | None

    The parameters of a named law held fixed by SciPy name, such as {'loc': 0}, or None to fit all.

    		 None
    simulations int

    The number of Monte Carlo samples of the null distribution of a named law.

    		 199
    random_state int | None

    The seed of the bootstrap of the power law and of the Monte Carlo samples of a named law.

    		 0

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    values_

    The pooled sample.
    labels_

    The label of every series.
    exponent_

    The exponent alpha of the density of the power law.
    minimum_

    The lower cutoff of the power law.
    maximum_

    The upper cutoff of the power law, or None without one.
    statistic_

    The Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance between the tail and the power law, or between the sample and a named law.
    p_value_

    For the power law, the share of bootstrap samples from the fit whose distance exceeds statistic_, or None without bootstrap, values above 0.1 not rejecting it. For a named law, the Monte Carlo p-value, values below the significance level rejecting it.
    tail_

    The number of samples between the cutoffs of the power law.
    comparisons_

    For every alternative of compare_with, the log-likelihood ratio of the power law against it, positive when the power law fits better, and its p-value.
    index_

    The stability index of the stable law, 2 for the normal law.
    skewness_

    The skewness of the stable law.
    shape_

    The shape xi of the extreme-value law, 0 for the Gumbel class, positive for the Fréchet class of heavy tails, and negative for the Weibull class of bounded tails.
    location_

    The location of the stable or the extreme-value law.
    scale_

    The scale of the stable or the extreme-value law.
    maxima_

    parameters_

    The fitted and fixed parameters of a named law.

    Examples:

    >>> import numpy as np
>>> from skcomplex.core.analysis import FitAnalysis
>>> samples = (1 - np.random.default_rng(0).random(5000)) ** (-1 / 1.5)
>>> round(FitAnalysis('power', minimum=1.0, bootstrap=0).prepare(samples).run().exponent_, 1)
2.5
>>> fit = FitAnalysis('exponential', fixed={'loc': 0})
>>> fit = fit.prepare(np.random.default_rng(0).exponential(2.0, 1000)).run()
>>> round(fit.parameters_['scale'], 0), fit.p_value_ > 0.05
(2.0, True)

    InformationAnalysis(kind='mutual', variables=None, *, symbols=None, bins=2, order=3, delay=1, history=1, lag=1, max_delay=100, dimension=8, estimator='plugin', k=3, base=2.0)

    Bases: BaseAnalysis

    Information among the series of a source, of one kind.

    The kinds measure pairs of series, every series, or all series together:

    • 'mutual': the mutual information H(X) + H(Y) - H(X, Y) of every pair of series, by plug-in counts.
    • 'transfer': the transfer entropy H(Y_t | Y_past) - H(Y_t | Y_past, X_{t-lag}) from every series to every series, the target conditioned on history past values, by plug-in counts or by the Kraskov-Stögbauer-Grassberger nearest-neighbour estimate of k neighbours.
    • 'kl-divergence': the Kullback-Leibler divergence of every series, a probability vector, from every series.
    • 'auto-mutual': the mutual information of every series with itself delayed by 0 to max_delay steps.
    • 'active-storage': the information the past history values of every series hold about its next value.
    • 'correlation-information': Lindgren's correlation information k_m = ΔS_{m-1} - ΔS_m of every series for block lengths 2 to dimension.
    • 'total-correlation', 'dual-total-correlation', 'o-information': the information all series share at any order, the information two or more of them share, and their difference, positive for redundancy and negative for synergy, by plug-in counts with dit, the closed form of a fitted Gaussian, or chains of neighbour estimates.
    • 'o-information-gradients': the O-information every series adds to the others.

    Every kind but 'kl-divergence' reads the series as symbols, or first turns them into symbols with symbols: 'bins' for bins bins of equal width, 'quantiles' for bins equally populated bins, or 'ordinal' for the rank pattern of every order values spaced by delay steps.

    		 None

    The number of symbols of bins and quantiles.

    		 2
    order int

    The length of ordinal patterns.

    		 3
    delay int

    The number of steps between the values of an ordinal pattern.

    		 1
    history int

    The number of past values of the target of the transfer entropy, or of the series of the storage.

    		 1
    lag int

    The delay of the source of the transfer entropy.

    		 1
    max_delay int

    The largest delay of the auto mutual information.

    		 100
    dimension int

    The largest block length of the correlation information.

    		 8
    estimator str

    'plugin' for counts of symbols, 'gaussian' for a fitted Gaussian, or 'knn' for nearest neighbours.

    		 'plugin'

>>> transfer = InformationAnalysis('transfer').prepare(np.column_stack([x, np.roll(x, 1)])).run()

    InvariantAnalysis(kind='conservation', *, expressions=(), symmetry=None, samples=16, random_state=None)

    Bases: BaseAnalysis

    Poisson brackets, conserved quantities, and symmetries of a system, with the Noether charge of a symmetry.

    The canonical pairs and the Hamiltonian H are those of the system's HamiltonianInteractions, whose Hamiltonians sum, and the Lagrangian L is the sum of those of its EulerLagrangeInteractions. The expressions are ObservableSpecs whose expression is a function of the namespace of the system, where s.<element>.<state> is the symbol of a state, or a symbolic expression of those symbols. The kinds:

    • 'brackets': the Poisson bracket {f, g} = sum df/dq dg/dp - df/dp dg/dq of every pair of expressions, summed over the canonical pairs.
    • 'conservation': the rate of change df/dt of every expression, which is diff(f, t) + {f, H} for a system whose dynamics all come from Hamiltonian interactions, and the Lie derivative along the vector field of its equations otherwise. An expression is conserved when its rate simplifies to zero, or, when simplification does not decide, when the rate vanishes within a tolerance at random states with the parameters at their values.
    • 'symmetry': whether the Hamiltonian, or else the Lagrangian, is unchanged to first order by the variation of a SymmetrySpec, and the Noether charge of the symmetry, sum p dq for a Hamiltonian and sum dL/dq' dq for a Lagrangian, with the variation of the velocities dq' = sum_j d(dq)/dq_j q_j'.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    kind str

    The analysis to run, one of the kinds above.

    		 'conservation'
    expressions Sequence[ObservableSpec]

    The expressions to bracket or to check.

    		 ()
    symmetry SymmetrySpec | None

    The symmetry to check.

    		 None
    samples int

    The number of random states of the numeric check.

    		 16
    random_state int | Generator | None

    The seed or generator of the random states.

    		 None

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    problem_

    The compiled problem.
    system_

    The system.
    dynamics_

    The first-order equations of the system, with the values of its parameters.
    namespace_

    The namespace of the symbols of the states and parameters of the system.
    brackets_

    A mapping from every pair of labels to the Poisson bracket of their expressions.
    rates_

    A mapping from every label to the rate of change of its expression.
    conserved_

    A mapping from every label to whether its expression is conserved.
    methods_

    A mapping from every label to the method that decided, 'symbolic' or 'numeric'.
    invariant_

    Whether the Hamiltonian or the Lagrangian is unchanged to first order by the symmetry.
    remainder_

    The first-order change of the Hamiltonian or the Lagrangian under the symmetry, zero when it is invariant.
    charge_

    The Noether charge of the symmetry.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    AnalysisError

    The source is not a system, the system is not an ODE, an expression or the symmetry is missing or invalid, or the system has no Hamiltonian interaction for brackets, or neither a Hamiltonian nor an Euler-Lagrange interaction for a symmetry.

    Examples:

    >>> from typing import Annotated
>>> from skcomplex.core.analysis import InvariantAnalysis
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.elements import Element
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.interactions import HamiltonianInteraction
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.system import System
>>> from skcomplex.core.specs import ObservableSpec, StateSpec
>>> class OscillatorElement(Element):
...     def __init__(self, label, q: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 1.0, p: Annotated[float, StateSpec()] = 0):
...         super().__init__(label)
...         self.q = q
...         self.p = p
>>> energy = lambda s: (s.target.p**2 + s.target.q**2) / 2
>>> system = System(
...     elements=[OscillatorElement('mass')],
...     interactions=[HamiltonianInteraction('spring', target='mass', hamiltonian=energy)],
... )
>>> expressions = [
...     ObservableSpec('energy', lambda s: s.mass.q**2 + s.mass.p**2),
...     ObservableSpec('position', lambda s: s.mass.q),
... ]
>>> analysis = InvariantAnalysis(expressions=expressions).prepare(system).run()
>>> analysis.conserved_
{'energy': True, 'position': False}
>>> analysis.rates_['position']
p_mass

    IrreversibilityAnalysis(kind='entropy-production', variables=None, *, rates=None, duration=None, drive=1.0, intensity=1.0, dt=1.0, n_states=None, significance=0.05, bins=40, entropy=None, resamples=200, random_state=None, unperturbed=None, field=1.0, correlation=None)

    Bases: BaseAnalysis

    Irreversibility of jump and Langevin dynamics, of one kind.

    The kinds read a rate matrix, jump paths, Langevin paths, samples, or ensembles:

    • 'entropy-production': the stationary entropy production rate of a jump process from its rate matrix, Σ_{i<j} (p_i k_ij - p_j k_ji) ln(p_i k_ij / (p_j k_ji)), 0 under detailed balance.
    • 'jump-entropy-production': the entropy every jump path produces in the medium, Σ ln(k_ij / k_ji) over its jumps with the rates, and the mean rate over the duration of the paths.
    • 'langevin-entropy-production': the entropy every overdamped Langevin path produces, the work of the drive times the intensity, b ∫ F(x) ∘ dx, and the mean rate.
    • 'count-entropy-production': the entropy production rate of a discrete path from its transition counts alone, Σ_{i<j} (N_ij - N_ji) ln(N_ij / N_ji) per unit time.
    • 'detailed-balance': the chi-squared test of detailed balance on the transition counts of discrete paths.
    • 'fluctuation-theorem': the log ratio of the probabilities of producing s and -s from samples of the entropy, and its slope against s, 1 when the theorem holds.
    • 'uncertainty-relation': the squared relative fluctuation Var(J) / ⟨J⟩² of samples of an integrated current times the mean entropy produced over the same duration, at least 2 (Barato and Seifert 2015).
    • 'response': the integrated response chi(t) = (<x(t)>_h - <x(t)>_0) / h of an ensemble with the field against the unperturbed ensemble.
    • 'fluctuation-dissipation': the response, and the slope of chi / b against C(t_w, t_w) - C(t, t_w) of the two-time correlation over the same lags, 1 in equilibrium and below 1 in an aging system.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    kind str

    The measure to compute, one of the kinds above.

    The discrete state or the position of a trajectory to read, or None for the first one.

    		 1.0
    intensity float

    The factor b of the work of the drive in the entropy, and one over the factor of the response in the fluctuation-dissipation ratio, as in the acceptance exp(-intensity * change) of sampling.

    		 1.0
    dt float

    The time between frames of Langevin paths, or between records of a discrete path.

    		 1.0
    n_states int | None

    The number of states, or None for the largest state plus one.

    		 None
    significance float

    		 0.05
    bins int

    The number of bins of entropy, symmetric about 0.

    		 40
    entropy float | None

    The mean entropy produced along a path over the duration of the currents.

    		 None
    resamples int

    		 200
    random_state int | None

    The seed of the bootstrap.

    		 None
    unperturbed ArrayLike | None

    		 None
    field float

    		 1.0
    correlation ArrayLike | None

    		 None

    LargeDeviationAnalysis(kind='tilted', variables=None, *, weights=None, tilts=1.0, values=None, block=10, dt=1.0, observable=None, population=1000, interval=1.0, until=20.0, random_state=None, simulation=None, bins=41, value_range=None, log_weights=None)

    Bases: BaseAnalysis

    Large deviations of a time-additive observable or of an order parameter, of one kind.

    The kinds estimate the scaled cumulant generating function lambda(k) at the tilts, or the rate function I:

    • 'tilted': exactly, for a counting observable of a jump process that adds weights[i, j] at every jump from i to j, as the largest eigenvalue of the tilted generator rates * exp(k weights) - diag(escape rates) of the rate matrix. A diagonal rate counts jumps that keep the state, such as the events of a Poisson process.
    • 'block': from blocks of block steps of one long run of the increments of the observable, as ln <exp(k A)> / (block dt).
    • 'cloning': by the fixed-population cloning of Giardinà, Kurchan, and Peliti, which advances every clone of a system by interval through the simulation's steppers, weights it by exp(k A) for the increment A of the observable, and resamples the population by the weights. The system is compiled once, and every segment restarts the clock at zero, so the laws must not depend on time explicitly. A warning names a population whose effective size falls below a tenth of the clones or below 10 clones.
    • 'histogram': the rate function of P_N(m) ≍ exp(-N I(m)) from the samples of an order parameter at several sizes N, fitting -ln P_N linearly in N in every bin.
    • 'reweight': samples reweighted to another law by the logarithms of the likelihood ratios, such as beta dh M.

    With values, the generating function kinds also give the rate function, its Legendre transform I(a) = max_k (k a - lambda(k)) over the tilts.

    LinearizationAnalysis(controls=None, outputs=None, at=None, *, state_weights=None, control_weights=None)

    Bases: BaseAnalysis

    Linear state-space system x' = A x + B u, y = C x + D u of a system near an operating point.

    The matrices are the Jacobians of the rates and of the outputs, derived symbolically and evaluated at the operating point. The controls are adaptive parameters, named by their dotted names, and the outputs are states or controls. The system is controllable when the rank of [B, AB, ..., A^(n-1) B] equals the number of states, and observable when the rank of [C; CA; ...; C A^(n-1)] does. With weights of the states and the controls, the gain K of the linear-quadratic regulator u = -K x minimises ∫ (x' Q x + u' R u) dt over an infinite horizon, from the continuous algebraic Riccati equation that SciPy solves.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    controls Sequence[str] | None

    The dotted names of the adaptive parameters that are inputs, or None for the bounded ones.

    		 None
    outputs Sequence[str] | None

    		 None
    at Mapping[str, float] | None

    The values of states and controls at the operating point, by dotted name, or None for the initial values.

    		 None
    state_weights ArrayLike | None

    The weight Q of the states in the cost of the regulator, a symmetric positive semidefinite matrix, or None for no regulator.

    		 None
    control_weights ArrayLike | None

    The weight R of the controls in the cost of the regulator, a symmetric positive definite matrix, or None for no regulator.

    		 None

    problem_

    The compiled problem.

    The state matrix, the Jacobian of the rates by the states.
    B_

    The input matrix, the Jacobian of the rates by the controls.

    LoopAnalysis(kind='loops', *, at=None, frame=-1, quantity=None)

    Bases: BaseAnalysis

    Feedback loops of the signed dependency graph of a system, their dominance in time, or its flow matrix.

    The signed dependency graph of a system has the state variables as nodes and an edge from x_j to x_i when the rate of x_i depends on x_j, with the sign of the partial derivative df_i/dx_j, the entry of the Jacobian. The rate of a map is the change of its state in one step, its next value minus itself. When a system declares flows, the flows are nodes too: an edge goes from each state to every flow whose amount depends on it, with the sign of the partial derivative, and from each flow to its sink with sign + and to its source with sign -, so the graph shows the path of every influence through the flows. Rate laws of single elements give the edges into the states they change, and the Jacobian, as StabilityAnalysis derives it with the parameters at their values, gives the edges into every other state, such as the members of a group or the velocity of a state of second order. Delays and smoothings pass their input with gain one.

    The kinds read a system or a trajectory:

    • 'loops': the signed dependency graph and its feedback loops, the elementary cycles of the graph found with Johnson's algorithm. The gain of a loop is the product of the partial derivatives along it, and its polarity the sign of the gain.
    • 'dominance': the gains of the loops along a trajectory, at every frame, and the dominant loop, with the largest absolute gain, at every frame.
    • 'flow-matrix': the transaction-flow matrix of one frame of a trajectory, with flows as rows and holders as columns. Every row holds the outflow of its flow at the source, negative, and the inflow at the sink, positive, so every row sums to zero. Flows of a group sum over its members. The matrix books the amounts the flows move between holders, which the Jacobian does not hold, so it is defined only for systems that declare flows.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    kind str

    The analysis of the loops, one of the kinds above.

    		 'loops'
    at ArrayLike | None

    The state vector the signs of 'loops' are evaluated at, or None for the initial state.

    		 None
    frame int

    The index of the frame of the flow matrix.

    		 -1
    quantity str | None

    The quantity whose flows form the rows of the flow matrix, or None for every flow.

    		 None

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    problem_

    The compiled problem.
    trajectory_

    The trajectory of 'dominance' and 'flow-matrix'.
    graph_

    The signed dependency graph from each state or flow to every node whose amount or rate depends on it, with the edge attributes sign and gain, for 'loops'. The members of a group and the components of a vector that the Jacobian describes are nodes of their own, named like species.x[0].
    loops_

    The nodes of every loop, in the order of their influence, starting at its first state by name, or at its first node by name when it holds no state.
    polarities_

    The polarity of every loop, at the first frame for 'dominance': 'reinforcing' for a positive product of edge signs, 'balancing' for a negative one, or 'neutral' when an edge has no influence.
    gains_

    The gain of every loop, with one row per frame for 'dominance'.
    times_

    The time of every frame of 'dominance'.
    dominant_

    The index of the loop with the largest absolute gain at every frame of 'dominance'.
    flows_

    The paths of the flows of the flow matrix.
    holders_

    The states and environments the flows connect.
    matrix_

    The outflow, negative, and the inflow, positive, of every flow for every holder.

    >>> from skcomplex.core.analysis import LoopAnalysis
>>> from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import Simulation
>>> from skcomplex.systems import create_system
>>> LoopAnalysis().prepare(create_system('bass_diffusion')).run().polarities_
['reinforcing', 'balancing']
>>> trajectory = Simulation(create_system('bass_diffusion'), dt=1).prepare().run(2).trajectory_
>>> LoopAnalysis('dominance').prepare(trajectory).run().gains_.shape
(3, 2)

    LyapunovAnalysis(kind='spectrum', variables=None, *, n_exponents=None, until=None, dt=None, transient=None, parameters=None, dimension=3, delay=1, min_separation=None, trajectory_length=20, skip=0)

    Bases: BaseAnalysis

    Lyapunov exponents of a system from its tangent dynamics, or the largest exponent of recorded series.

    The kinds read a system or data:

    • 'spectrum': the largest n_exponents exponents of a flow or a map from the system's initial state. The tangent dynamics use the symbolic Jacobian, in which abs(u) has the derivative sign(u), and the compiled functions take the parameters as an argument, so a sweep over parameter values compiles them once. Tangent vectors are re-orthonormalised by QR after every step, as in the Benettin algorithm, and the exponents are the average logarithmic growth of the diagonal of R. The Kaplan-Yorke dimension and the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy, by Pesin's identity the sum of the positive exponents, follow from the spectrum. An array of exponents passes through as the spectrum.
    • 'largest': Rosenstein's estimate of the largest exponent of every series, from the divergence of neighbours of its delay embedding.

    A positive largest exponent indicates chaos.

    MarkovAnalysis(kind='transition-matrix', variables=None, *, matrix=None, n_states=None, lag=1, lags=(1,), n_timescales=1, n_metastable=None, reversible=True, dt=1.0)

    Bases: BaseAnalysis

    Markov chain of discrete paths, or of a transition or rate matrix, of one kind.

    The kinds read the integer states of one path, or one row per path, or a matrix with matrix:

    • 'transition-matrix': the transitions after lag steps counted along the paths and normalized by row.
    • 'stationary': the stationary law pi of the matrix, pi P = pi or pi Q = 0 for rates.
    • 'spectral-gap': the gap 1 - |lambda_2|, or -Re lambda_2 for rates, and the relaxation time of every mode.
    • 'state-system': the maximum-likelihood Markov state model of the largest connected set, with its metastable sets found by PCCA+.
    • 'timescales': the slowest implied timescales of Markov state models at every lag of lags, which do not depend on the lag for a Markovian discretization.

    ModeDecompositionAnalysis(variables=None, *, rank=None, dictionary=None, inputs=None, validation=0.2, horizon=0, dt=1.0, label='surrogate')

    Bases: BaseAnalysis

    Linear system fitted to series by dynamic mode decomposition, computed with PyDMD.

    The decomposition fits the exact DMD of the one-sample map g(t + dt) = A g(t) to the pairs of consecutive samples of every run. With a dictionary, g holds the observables the dictionary computes from the variables, which is extended DMD, and the dictionary should keep the variables among its observables. The fitted system follows the rate law dg/dt = L g with L = Phi diag(ln(mu) / dt) Phi^+ under continuous time and starts at the first sample of the first run. The forecast iterates the map from the last sample of the last run.

    With inputs, the decomposition is dynamic mode decomposition with control, g(t + dt) = A g(t) + B u(t), where g holds the variables that are not inputs or their observables. The fitted system follows dg/dt = L g + M u, where M gives the same one-sample map under an input held over the sample. Every input is a bounded adaptive parameter of the surrogate element, bounded by its range in the samples, and the forecast holds the inputs at their last values.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    variables Sequence[str] | None

    The variables of trajectories, or None for every scalar state or observable. The inputs join them when they are not listed.

    		 None
    rank float | None

    The rank of the truncated singular value decomposition: a number of modes, 0 for the optimal hard threshold, a share of the energy below 1, or None to keep every singular value.

    		 None
    dictionary TransformerMixin | None

    A scikit-learn transformer that computes the observables, such as PolynomialFeatures(2), or None for the variables themselves.

    		 None
    inputs Sequence[str] | None

    The names of the variables that are control inputs, or None for none.

    		 None
    validation float

    The share of the samples of every run held out at its end to measure the validation error.

    		 0.2
    horizon int

    The number of samples to forecast after the last sample of the last run.

    		 0
    dt float

    The time between the rows of an array.

    		 1.0
    label str

    The label of the surrogate element.

    		 'surrogate'

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    samples_

    The series of every run, the names of the variables, and the step, set by prepare.
    system_

    The system of one surrogate element under continuous time, whose states follow dg/dt = L g + M u.
    labels_

    The variables, or the observables of the dictionary, in the order of the states.
    states_

    The names of the states of the surrogate element.
    last_state_

    The values of the states at the last sample of the last run, where the forecast starts.
    dt_

    The time between the samples it was fitted to.
    training_error_

    The relative error of the predicted increments over one sample on the training samples.
    validation_error_

    The relative error on the held-out samples, NaN when none are held out.
    eigenvalues_

    The continuous eigenvalues ln(mu) / dt of the modes, from the eigenvalues mu of the one-sample map.
    modes_

    The modes, one column per mode and one row per state.
    amplitudes_

    The amplitudes of the modes at the last sample of the last run.
    generator_

    The matrix L of the rate law, one row and one column per state.
    input_generator_

    The matrix M of the rate law, one row per state and one column per input.
    operator_

    The matrix A of the one-sample map, one row and one column per state.
    input_matrix_

    The matrix B of the one-sample map, one row per state and one column per input.
    dictionary_

    forecast_

    Examples:

    >>> import numpy as np
>>> from skcomplex.core.analysis import ModeDecompositionAnalysis
>>> times = np.arange(0.0, 10.0, 0.1)
>>> values = np.column_stack([np.cos(times), np.sin(times)])
>>> analysis = ModeDecompositionAnalysis(['x', 'y'], horizon=5, dt=0.1).prepare(values).run()
>>> np.sort(analysis.eigenvalues_.imag).round(6).tolist()
[-1.0, 1.0]
>>> bool(np.allclose(analysis.forecast_[:, 0], np.cos(times[-1] + 0.1 * np.arange(1, 6))))
True
>>> u = np.random.default_rng(0).uniform(-1.0, 1.0, 100)
>>> x = np.zeros(100)
>>> for k in range(99):
...     x[k + 1] = 0.9 * x[k] + 0.5 * u[k]
>>> analysis = ModeDecompositionAnalysis(['x', 'u'], inputs=['u'], validation=0.0)
>>> analysis = analysis.prepare(np.column_stack([x, u])).run()
>>> analysis.operator_.round(6).tolist(), analysis.input_matrix_.round(6).tolist()
([[0.9]], [[0.5]])

    NeighborAnalysis(kind='distances', group=None, *, variables=None, box=None, bins=100, r_max=None, attribute='state', empty=None, diagonal=True)

    Bases: BaseAnalysis

    Neighbours of agents in space, or of cells of a grid or nodes of a network, of one kind.

    The kinds read positions, or states on grids and networks:

    • 'distances': the distance from every agent to its nearest neighbour, across periodic edges in a box.
    • 'clark-evans': the mean nearest-neighbour distance over its value for uniform random points in a periodic box, 1 for random points, below 1 for clustered ones, and up to 2.15 for a triangular lattice in a plane.
    • 'radial-distribution': the radial distribution function g(r) in a periodic box, averaged over frames, 1 for an ideal gas.
    • 'like-share': the mean share of an agent's occupied neighbours that share its state, on a periodic grid or along the edges of a network, near 1 when segregated.

    An array of positions holds one snapshot, one row per agent, or one snapshot per frame along its first axis. A trajectory gives the positions of an agent group with the sides of its periodic space as the box, or its lattice frames for 'like-share'. A grid array is one frame of states, and a graph carries the states on its nodes.

    NetworkAnalysis(kind='summary', *, orders=(1, 2), attribute=None, numeric=False, measure='degree', method='louvain', reference=None, random_state=None)

    Bases: BaseAnalysis

    Measures of the network of every frame of a trajectory, or of a graph, of one kind.

    The kinds read the graph of every frame:

    • 'degrees': the degree of every node, the moments <k^n> of the degree distribution for every order of orders, and the fitted exponent of a heavy-tailed degree distribution, nan below 50 nodes or for a narrow one.
    • 'assortativity': the assortativity by degree, or by a node attribute, positive when linked nodes are alike.
    • 'centrality': the degree, betweenness, closeness, eigenvector, or PageRank centrality of every node.
    • 'communities': the communities by Louvain modularity maximization or label propagation, their modularity, and their agreement with a reference partition.
    • 'neighbor-degree': the mean degree of the neighbours of nodes against their degree, rising in assortative networks.
    • 'summary': the size, mean degree, clustering, path length, diameter, and components, with the path measures on the largest component.

    OperatorAnalysis(kind='spectrum', *, n_states=6, parameters=None, sector=None, subsystems=None)

    Bases: BaseAnalysis

    Spectrum and ground state of an operator system, or the purity and entanglement of the states of its trajectory.

    The kinds read a system or a trajectory:

    • 'spectrum': the lowest eigenvalues and eigenstates of the generator, by exact diagonalisation. QuTiP diagonalises small spaces densely and larger ones with a sparse eigensolver. A sector restricts the basis to the states with a given eigenvalue of a conserved operator that is diagonal in the product basis, such as the total magnetisation.
    • 'ground-state': the lowest eigenvalue and eigenstate of the generator.
    • 'purity': the purity Tr(rho^2) of the state of a trajectory at every frame, 1 for pure states.
    • 'entanglement': the von Neumann entropy of the reduced state of some subsystems at every frame of a trajectory, in nats.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    kind str

    		 'spectrum'

    Parameter values by dotted name that replace the initial ones.

    		 None
    sector SectorSpec | None

    The sector of a conserved diagonal operator whose basis states the spectrum keeps, or None for every basis state.

    		 None
    subsystems Sequence[str] | None

    The keys of the subsystems to keep, such as chain[0], or the path of a whole element or group.

    		 None

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    problem_

    The compiled operator problem.
    trajectory_

    The trajectory of 'purity' and 'entanglement'.
    energies_

    The eigenvalues of the spectrum in increasing order.
    states_

    The eigenstates of the spectrum as columns over the whole space.
    energy_

    The ground state energy.
    state_

    The ground state vector.
    purity_

    The purity at every frame.
    entropy_

    The entanglement entropy at every frame.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    AnalysisError

    The system or the trajectory holds no operators, the sector operator is not diagonal or lacks the eigenvalue, or a subsystem is not part of the trajectory.
    ParameterError

    A parameter name is not part of the system.

    Examples:

    >>> from typing import Annotated
>>> import numpy as np
>>> from sage.all__sagemath_symbolics import CC, SR
>>> from skcomplex.core.analysis import OperatorAnalysis
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.elements import Element, GroupElement
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.laws import GeneratorLaw
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.laws.utils import local_operator
>>> from skcomplex.core.specs import HilbertSpec, StateSpec
>>> from skcomplex.core.components.system import System
>>> from skcomplex.core.engine.compile import OperatorCompiler
>>> from skcomplex.core.engine.runtime import Simulation
>>> operators = {'z': (np.diag([1, -1]), True), 'minus': (np.array([[0, 0], [1, 0]]), False)}
>>> QUBIT = HilbertSpec(2, operators, basis={'up': 0, 'down': 1})
>>> class TwoLevelElement(Element):
...     def __init__(
...         self, label, psi: Annotated[object, StateSpec(domain=CC**2)] = 'up', hilbert=QUBIT
...     ):
...         super().__init__(label)
...         self.psi = psi
...         self.hilbert = hilbert
...
...     def _get_laws(self, s):
...         return [GeneratorLaw(local_operator(s.psi, SR.symbol('z')))]
>>> system = System(elements=[TwoLevelElement('q')])
>>> OperatorAnalysis(n_states=2).prepare(system).run().energies_.round(6).tolist()
[-1.0, 1.0]
>>> singlet = np.array([0, 1, -1, 0]) / np.sqrt(2)
>>> pair = System(elements=[GroupElement('pair', element=TwoLevelElement, size=2)])
>>> trajectory = Simulation(
...     pair, compiler=OperatorCompiler(), dt=1.0, initial_state={'system.state': singlet},
... ).prepare().run(until=1.0).trajectory_
>>> analysis = OperatorAnalysis('entanglement', subsystems=['pair[0]']).prepare(trajectory).run()
>>> bool(np.allclose(analysis.entropy_, np.log(2)))
True

    PassageAnalysis(kind='first-passage', variables=None, *, threshold=None, target=None, origin=None, direction='up', level=0.0, lag=1, dt=1.0)

    Bases: BaseAnalysis

    Passages of paths to a level or a set of states, or of a Markov chain between two sets, of one kind.

    The kinds read paths, one row per path on common times, or a transition matrix:

    • 'first-passage': the first time every path reaches threshold, from below for direction='up' and from above for 'down', or enters the target states.
    • 'hitting': the share of paths that reach each of the absorbing target states before the others.
    • 'return-times': the times between successive returns of a series to level, by visit or by crossing.
    • 'committor': the forward committor of a transition matrix, the probability that the chain reaches the target states before the origin states.
    • 'mean-first-passage': the mean first-passage time of a transition matrix at lag from the origin states, started in their stationary weights, to the target states.

    The matrix kinds estimate the transition matrix at lag of the jump path of a trajectory.

    Parameters:

    threshold float | None

    The level a first passage reaches.

    		 None

    The states that end a passage, the absorbing states, or the target set of the chain.

    The origin set of the chain.

    direction str

    'up' to reach values at or above the threshold, 'down' at or below it.

    		 'up'
    level float

    The level of the returns.

    		 0.0
    lag int

    The lag of the transition matrix in steps.

    		 1
    dt float

    The time of one step of an array, while a trajectory gives its own times.

    		 1.0

>>> passage = PassageAnalysis(threshold=2).prepare([[0, 1, 2, 3], [0, 0, 0, 0]]).run()
>>> passage.passage_times_.tolist()
[2.0, nan]
